hook: Greg Brockman helped write OpenAI's founding announcement in December 2015 and has run its engineering effort ever since, first as chief technology officer and then, from November 2023, as president. Before that he left MIT to join Stripe in its earliest days, when the payments company was still called dev slash payments, and stayed through its rise into a major engineering organization as chief technology officer. He testified to the Senate about AI policy as early as November 2016, years before the topic reached the mainstream, and he was reinstated as OpenAI's president within days of the company's November 2023 board crisis.

standing.watch: What is unresolved according to the records is the cluster of cases naming OpenAI entities, none of which yet shows a development beyond filing. These include TradeSun, Inc. v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, Bass v. OpenAI, LLC, United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC, JIANG v. OPENAI GROUP PBC, Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, GRANT v. OPENAI INC, and Vredenburgh v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, all with docket monitoring active and no development recorded. One case on the site, Buist v. Anthropic, PBC, names a different company and is not tied to Brockman in these records. The records do not show a pending listing, a planned financing, or any other corporate event for OpenAI beyond the November 2023 leadership announcement. Because the records are thin on outcomes, the next thing to watch is simply whether any of these dockets move.
standing.record: The site's records add up to a career built at two companies and a long public record on AI policy. He co-founded OpenAI in December 2015 and served as its first chief technology officer, then became president, a title confirmed in the November 29, 2023 leadership announcement. His earlier engineering career ran through Stripe, which he joined in its earliest days when it was still called dev slash payments and where he stayed as chief technology officer until May 8, 2015. The coverage also notes his 2007 Intel Science Talent Search placement, sixth, for a paper on Ducci sequences, and peer-reviewed papers on combinatorics including work on universal cycles of labeled graphs. The pattern running through the records is a technical founder who moved from payments infrastructure into the leadership of an AI lab and stayed there through its internal crisis. The lawsuits on this site name OpenAI entities rather than Brockman himself, and most are recorded only as filed with docket monitoring active and no development yet.
standing.standing: Greg Brockman stands as president and co-founder of OpenAI, the company he helped announce in December 2015 and whose engineering effort he has run since, first as chief technology officer and then as president from November 2023. The records show he was reinstated as president within days of the November 2023 board crisis, and that his title was confirmed in the company's November 29, 2023 leadership announcement. He is listed on this site as both a founder and an executive of OpenAI, which places him among the people who control and influence the organization. Before OpenAI he left MIT to join Stripe in its earliest days, when it was still called dev slash payments, and stayed as chief technology officer until May 8, 2015. He also testified to the Senate Commerce Committee on artificial intelligence policy on November 30, 2016, years before the topic reached the mainstream.
